item.text: The searches recovered a few usable target-period records and several negative/blocked results. I’m now checking the underlying pages for exact dates, sections, and whether the claim is a finding, an official act, or only contextual/contested material before assigning new units.

Continuation research completed across all eight chapters. No scores, ranges, rankings, or judge advice were assigned.

The repository remains read-only: shell access failed with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`, so I could not append `research-materials.md` or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following handoff preserves provisional numbering after E034.

### 1B — Nuclear / existential risk

- **E035** — Thailand’s 2022 Prevention and Suppression of Torture and Enforced Disappearance Act was published in the Royal Gazette on 25 October and countersigned by Prayut. Locator: *The Nation*, 26 October 2022, lines 8–20. Maps: `1B.10`, `3B.7`, `8B.1`. This is a formal rights/safeguards act, not nuclear evidence. Its delayed 120-day commencement limits target-year effectiveness. [Source](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/politics/40021414)

The IAEA 2022 statement was located but could not be reliably opened; it remains discovery-only. No ruler-specific nuclear, biological, delivery-system, proliferation, or crisis-conduct evidence was recovered.

### 2B — International peace

- **E036** — Reuters reported that Thailand’s government delegation maintained the BRN truce during April 2022 despite PULO bombings, with talks continuing toward a political solution. Locator: Reuters/Euronews, 18 April 2022, lines 603–616. Maps: `2B.1`, `2B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. Attribution is institutional through the government negotiating team, not personal direction by Prayut. Contrary evidence: two explosions killed one civilian and injured three police officers, and PULO objected that the talks were insufficiently inclusive. [Source](https://www.euronews.com/2022/04/18/us-thailand-insurgency)

The search did not recover reliable 2022 operational-command, cross-border coercion, proxy-control, or accountability records. Chapter remains materially incomplete.

### 3B — Domestic safety

- **E037** — WHO’s April 2022 Universal Health Preparedness Review examined Thailand’s pandemic response through 13 site visits, six high-level meetings, interviews, and simulations. It identified whole-of-society coordination but also limited provincial capacity requiring reinforcement. Maps: `3B.7`, `3B.10`, `6B.1`, `6B.9`, `8B.2`. This is institutional outcome evidence, not direct Prayut attribution. [Source](https://www.who.int/thailand/news/detail/12-05-2022-thailand-shares-lessons-learned-from-the-covid-19-pandemic-with-who)

The torture-law record above supplies a formal remedy act, but no target-period complaint outcomes, prison evidence, independent investigations, or proof of effective enforcement were found. The chapter’s adverse evidence remains stronger than its favorable and corrective evidence.

### 4B — Political freedom

- **E038** — OECD’s 2022 review found that Thailand lacked an agreed national open-government strategy and recommended clearer institutional responsibility, monitoring, public consultation, information access, and stronger independence for the information commission. Locator: OECD report, executive-summary recommendations, lines 3719–3778. Maps: `4B.5`, `4B.7`, `4B.10`, `8B.3`, `8B.8`. This is an external institutional assessment; it does not prove Prayut personally rejected reforms. [Source](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/open-and-connected-government-review-of-thailand_e1593a0c-en.html)

No new 2022 appointment, Election Commission independence, digital-control, or opposition-outcome evidence was recovered. The term-limit ruling remains the strongest precise institutional record.

### 5B — Economic wellbeing

- **E039** — The World Bank’s October 2022 rural-income diagnostic found that 79% of Thailand’s poor lived in rural areas, with poverty especially high in the South and Northeast; rural household income averaged about 68% of urban income. Locator: World Bank press release, lines 142–151. Maps: `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `6B.6`. This establishes distributional exposure and policy need, not Prayut’s personal causation. Contrary evidence: Thailand had achieved major long-run poverty reduction, but progress had slowed and COVID effects remained uneven. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/10/21/rural-thailand-faces-the-largest-poverty-challenges-with-high-income-inequality)

- **E040** — Thailand’s DSI searched five locations in July 2022 concerning alleged collusive bidding on post-office construction and seized procurement and computer records. Locator: DSI report, lines 74–78. Maps: `5B.5`, `7B.6`, `8B.5`. This confirms an investigation, not wrongdoing or a Prayut nexus; names of alleged offenders were not disclosed. [Source](https://www.dsi.go.th/en/Detail/ccd2b44af7ab4ba78291cf3c03e54638)

No personal asset, appointment, competition/capture, or independently evaluated policy-implementation evidence was recovered.

### 6B — Social wellbeing

- **E041** — WHO reported that Thailand’s 2022 migrant-vaccination program covered documented and undocumented migrants through free vaccination, multilingual outreach, mobile services, and migrant-health volunteers; 1,186 migrants had been vaccinated by the report date. Locator: WHO, 23 March 2022, lines 62–78. Maps: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.7`, `6B.10`. Contrary evidence: the program was collaborative and externally supported, so direct Prayut ownership and national affordability/quality effects remain unestablished. [Source](https://www.who.int/thailand/news/detail/23-03-2022-thailand-s-migrant-vaccination-programme-ensures-no-one-is-left-behind)

The WHO review also documented migrant and provincial-capacity constraints. No durable education, service-quality, regional-outcome, or post-period institutional evidence was recovered.

### 7B — Personal integrity

No admissible new target-period personal-integrity unit was recovered.

- The NACC/asset-declaration searches did not retrieve Prayut’s actual 2022 declaration or a verified beneficial-interest, family-benefit, correction, obstruction, or independent personal finding.
- The DSI procurement record remains institutional context only.
- Searches involving Prawit Wongsuwan and other officials were rejected as non-attributable to Prayut.

Chapter 7B remains the principal attribution blocker.

### 8B — Effectiveness

- **E042** — Thailand’s official APEC 2022 site records Prayut presiding over the BCG exhibition opening on 14 November 2022 and identifies the APEC leadership agenda and implementation framework. Locator: official APEC Thailand site, lines 103–126. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`, `8B.10`. This establishes visible program leadership, not successful domestic implementation. [Source](https://www.apec2022.go.th/)

- **E043** — APEC’s 18 November 2022 release records Prayut’s advocacy of the BCG model as Thailand’s domestic recovery and long-term development strategy. Locator: APEC release, lines 389–402. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`. Contrary evidence: the statement is aspirational and contains no budget, milestone, evaluation, or durable-outcome evidence. [Source](https://www.apec.org/press/news-releases/2022/apec-leaders-rally-behind-sustainability-agenda-for-future-growth)

- **E044** — The OECD’s 2022 review found missing national open-government coordination and recommended monitoring, institutional clarification, public consultation, and stronger information access. Maps: `8B.3`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`. This supplies implementation-capacity contrary evidence, not a personal failure finding. [Source](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/open-and-connected-government-review-of-thailand_e1593a0c-en.html)

The chapter now has concrete portfolio and coordination evidence, but budgets, appointments, milestones, correction/replacement, and durable outcomes remain incomplete.

### Disposition changes

- **Retained:** E035–E044, with the attribution and temporal limitations stated above.
- **Rejected/discovery-only:** the inaccessible IAEA 2022 statement; unretrieved NACC asset-declaration material; non-Prayut cases involving other officials.
- **Still excluded:** the blocked Crisis Group source and incomplete Thai MFA/APEC candidates from the prior pass.

The evidence remains suitable for downstream cautious interpretation, with missing evidence treated as uncertainty rather than negative ruler evidence.
